newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to meet Balladur in French reconciliation.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to meet Balladur in French reconciliation.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will meet former prime minister Edouard Balladur on Wednesday for only their second private meeting since the two Gaullists clashed for the presidency in 1995, Chirac's office said.
The meeting appeared intended to seal the reconciliation of France's centre-right camp in the run-up to a snap parliamentary election called by Chirac for May 25 and June 1.

Balladur, who has stayed away from most coalition and Gaullist party gatherings since Chirac defeated him for the presidency, was given pride of place on the platform on Tuesday when Prime Minister Alain Juppe outlined the government's policy agenda for the election.

Juppe, who described the state of public finances on taking office in May 1995 as "calamitous", went out of his way to praise Balladur's record in his speech, saying the coalition could be proud of its achievements.
Balladur's chief lieutenant, Nicolas Sarkozy, has also been rehabilitated, attending a coalition leaders' lunch at Juppe's office on Tuesday.

However, two senior politicians who supported Chirac in the presidential campaign -- free-marketeer Alain Madelin and anti-Maastricht campaigner Philippe Seguin -- showed their differences at the outset.

Madelin failed to show up for Juppe's keynote speech, leaving an embarassing empty chair on the platform. Seguin was at the speech but did not attend the coalition lunch and let it be known he had not approved of calling an early election.
